summary:
MARS: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive engineering simulation that allows users to manage a research base on Mars. Players act as mission commanders responsible for keeping a four-person crew alive throughout a 30-Sol mission.

The simulation connects essential life-support systems, including oxygen, water, food, electrical power, thermal control, radiation exposure, and equipment maintenance. Players make resource-management decisions, respond to system failures and environmental events, and observe how their decisions affect the mission over time.

The project aims to make the engineering challenges of long-duration Mars exploration more understandable through an interactive, decision-based learning experience.
details:
MARS is an interactive Mars base management and engineering simulation designed to demonstrate the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars.

The user takes the role of a mission commander managing a four-person crew over a 30-Sol mission. The simulation includes interconnected life-support and engineering systems: oxygen production and consumption, water recycling, food supplies, solar power generation, battery storage, thermal regulation, radiation exposure, and equipment maintenance.

Each Martian day, the commander reviews available resources, adjusts system priorities, manages resource production and processing, and responds to environmental events and equipment failures. Decisions have consequences that affect resource availability and the ability to sustain the mission.

The project provides an interactive 3D Mars research base and mission dashboards to help users understand the engineering, resource-management, and operational challenges of future human exploration of Mars.

The application was developed as a web-based interactive simulation using modern web development technologies, with a dedicated simulation engine and a 3D visualization environment.
